question: Skeletal tuberculosis characteristically presents with a rapid, high-grade fever and acute-onset joint pain similar to pyogenic septic arthritis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect — the statement is FALSE. Skeletal TB is indolent: low-grade or absent fever, constitutional symptoms (evening rise of temperature, weight loss, night sweats), and months-long history. Pyogenic infections present acutely with high fever and rapid deterioration.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. Skeletal TB is an indolent infection with low-grade or absent fever, chronic insidious onset over weeks to months, and gradual joint destruction, in sharp contrast to the acute high fever and rapid joint destruction of pyogenic septic arthritis.
